objective: Complete the Packages owner surface over its partial backend in both directions: an immutable release that carries its dependencies, the extension_application registration the plane refused by name, the serving binding that earns launchability from the DomainApp runtime that serves, and the affected-System impact a recall records — with recall landing with the registry and a composed done-bar over the whole lifecycle.
falsifiable_claim: Slice A: POST /v1/hypervisor/packages/:id/releases admits a v2 HypervisorSurfaceReleaseRecord whose dependency_release_refs resolve at admission (unknown, foreign-owner and recalled refs refuse by name) and are bound into the release digest. Slice B: POST .../installations/:installation_id/registration admits exactly one v2 HypervisorApplicationSurfaceRegistration per installed binding on an active release, derived from admitted truth (class extension_application, route /__ioi/extensions/{package_id}, origin organization, effect boundary from the release's depth, contracts = the binding's allowed subsets), appends the binding's enabled successor revision under the caller's exact head, and the compiled product-surface join reads registered extensions as a second registration source so their typed reason is exactly no_serving_binding. npm run check:packages-journey --workspace=@ioi/hypervisor-app drives all of it against an isolated daemon and serve lane. Slice C: POST .../installations/:installation_id/serving-binding admits exactly one v2 HypervisorSurfaceServingBinding per registered, enabled binding, DERIVED from the package's own DomainApp runtime — which must be mounted and serving through the DomainApp plane's governed ladder (a merely mounted runtime, another DomainApp's runtime, and a second binding refuse by name) — copying that runtime's internal route; the compiled join reads registered extensions' serving bindings with the operational state re-read from the runtime ladder on every projection, so launchable:true with resolved_launch_route = the runtime's route appears on the next read after serve and stop-serving withdraws it on the next read with no registry mutation; /__ioi/extensions/<key> follows the join's answer (302 to the resolved route) or names the join's typed reasons (409). Slice D: the recall successor carries a registered HypervisorPackageRecallImpact v1 DERIVED at the recall admission — the installations over the release with their registration and live serving state, the Systems the DomainApp plane binds the serving apps to, the releases whose dependency_release_refs name the recalled release, and stop_serving/unmount handoffs to the DomainApp plane — bounded to the recaller's tenants and saying so; a recall stops nothing (the runtime reads serving afterwards) and cascades to no dependent (it stays active). node scripts/check-packages-product-lifecycle.mjs composes the route tests, the packages journey, the registry smoke, the product-surface compiler and the contract bar on ONE basis with no absence and no scheduled leg (exit 0 or 1).

The golden fixture bar was proven to evaluate the new v2 negatives by making one valid and watching check:architecture-contracts go red. Slice C: package_registry_routes::tests 11/11 — canon's operational enum is a function of the runtime ladder (serving; degraded when the ladder says serving without a route; stopped; ready; inactive; blocked; unavailable for a runtime this projection cannot read), the reason codes name the stages that failed and an empty answer is eligibility, the derived record satisfies the v2 contract, and a non-serving or route-less runtime is refused by name. The packages journey (78/78, first run) binds before serve (refused), anonymously (refused), to another runtime (refused), then binds, replays, refuses a second binding, follows resolved_launch_route to the served view and the canonical route's 302, stops serving and reads launchability withdrawn in the binding, the installation, the join and the canonical route (409), serves again and reads it restored, then re-pins the recall cascade, restart and uninstall with the admitted serving binding present. The golden fixture bar was proven to evaluate the new v2 negatives by making one valid and watching check:architecture-contracts go red. Slice D: package_registry_routes::tests 12/12 — the impact over one installation, one dependent release, no System and no handoff, with the nonclaims present, and an outsider identity reaching no installation while still seeing the dependent. The packages journey (83/83) cuts a dependent release, recalls, and asserts the frozen impact (registered + serving installation with its runtime ref, the dependent by ref, the DomainApp plane's stop-serving and unmount handoffs), that the runtime still serves and the dependent stays active after the recall, the release page's rendering, and the impact's survival across restart. The composed gate's first run: 7 executed clause checks green on one basis; its --mutation self-drill fails a planted red clause.
remaining_nonclaims: No health observation plane exists in this estate: health_observation_refs is empty on every serving binding, and the operational state is the DomainApp runtime's admitted ladder state (surface_operational_state_source: domain_app_runtime_ladder), not a liveness probe of the served bytes.

The DomainApp inventory-status projection still carries surface_registration_ref and package_release_ref as nulls; they are that plane's owner-authored fields and the package plane does not write them.

No HypervisorSystemInterfaceBinding plane exists yet; a recall's affected Systems are derived from the serving DomainApps' owner-authored system_binding_refs (empty in every journey), and the record says the reach is bounded to the recaller's tenants.
Deprecation, supersession and revocation remain unbuilt: recall is the family's one disposition successor, and the impact record is derived for it alone.

Registration enables the organization's installation binding and the serving binding names the runtime that serves it; the registry starts no process, serves no bytes of its own, binds no System, stops no runtime and grants no authority.
